newsitem.title: USA: Bill offered to have independent US EPA ombudsman.
newsitem.headline: Bill offered to have independent US EPA ombudsman.

text.p: A Missouri Republican said Friday he will offer a bill in the House of Representatives to establish an independment ombudsman to help communities file grievances against the Environmental Protection Agency.
Rep. Jim Talent said his bill would give the ombudsman a statutory basis and make the person separate from the agency he is supposed to monitor and investigate.
"This legislation guarantees the integrity of the Office of Ombudsman and allows whoever holds that office to act as a full and fair judge of the agency's behavior," Talent said.

At the urging of citizens of Times Beach, a city in his district with the nation's second-largest Superfund site, Talent asked the current EPA ombudsman to review problems the community was having with the EPA over a waste incinerator.
But Talent said he found the ombudsman could not be effective.
"As long as the ombudsman is at the mercy of the people running the agency, we can't expect a full and fair independent analysis," he said.
Talent said he hoped to attach his bill to a Superfund hazardous waste site reauthorization bill or the EPA funding bill for next year, or move it independently.
